item.title: PSG's Kvaratskhelia season in doubt after torn ACL
item.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an ACL injury during Paris Saint-Germain's win against Barcelona (JULIEN DE ROSA) Paris Saint-Germain could be without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the season after the winger tore his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona and Ousmane Dembele faces weeks out too, the club said on Wednesday. Both players suffered the injuries in the reigning European champions' 4-2 league phase win against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. "Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday's match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days," PSG said in a statement, without giving a timeline for his recovery. Recovery from ACL surgery typically takes between six and nine months, meaning the 25-year-old Georgia international can at best hope to return for the closing stages of the season. Former Napoli winger Kvaratskhelia has established himself as one of Europe's most exciting attacking players and played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles in the last two seasons. Like Dembele, he is one of the contenders for the Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded on Monday. The club said Dembele, the current Ballon d'Or holder, and influential Brazilian central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for "several weeks" with thigh injuries they suffered in the win against Barcelona. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark on Tuesday. Dembele, 29, had to be substituted after 20 minutes due to his injury. In the absence of two of their attacking stars, PSG will need to rely on summer signings Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, the Spain international who scored the winning goal in the World Cup final in July. PSG are away to Ligue 1 leaders Lyon on Sunday in their next domestic match and they travel to Spanish side Villarreal for their next Champions League fixture on November 3. ali-rbo/gj/nf

item.title: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery after tearing ACL in PSG win over Barcelona
item.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery after tearing ACL in PSG win over Barcelona Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has torn the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery, leaving the European champions without one of their most decisive attackers. The 25-year-old, who was named the Champions League's best player last season and is a nominee for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, was injured in Tuesday's 4-2 home win over Barcelona. The Georgia international landed awkwardly while challenging Barcelona full-back Xavi Espart just before the hour mark. He was helped off in the 59th minute and replaced by Maghenes Akliouche, with Espart and PSG teammate Desire Doue both trying to console him as he left the pitch. PSG said on Wednesday the operation will take place "in the coming days" but gave no recovery timeline, though it's likely the winger's season is over. "Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days," the club statement said. Kvaratskhelia joined PSG from Napoli in January 2025 and has scored 29 goals and provided 20 assists in 91 games for the club, playing an integral role in their back-to-back Champions League triumphs. Summer signing Mika Godts looks the likeliest candidate to replace Kvaratskhelia on the left wing, while Ferran Torresm, Ousmane Dembele and Akliouche offer alternative options. Dembele and Marquinhos also sidelined Kvaratskhelia was not the only casualty against Barcelona. Reigning Ballon d'Or holder Dembele went off with a left thigh injury in the 20th minute and was replaced by Torres, while captain Marquinhos hurt his right thigh soon after Kvaratskhelia's exit and made way for Ilya Zabarnyi. According to the club's statement, both players "will remain under treatment for the next few weeks". PSG, who are second in Ligue 1

item.title: Texas football fan banned after flipping off Florida players on field after UT loss
item.description: Florida players engaged in a postgame spat with a rowdy Texas football fan after Florida's 27-24 win in Austin on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. (Tim Warner/Getty Images) Texas football 's home contest against Florida last Saturday brought two losses for one Longhorns fan. Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) dropped its second straight game in a 27-24 defeat to the Gators, a surprising home loss that featured one additional moment of drama postgame. One person wearing a burnt orange polo was caught on video flipping his middle finger to a collection of Florida players. While some of the student-athletes laughed oof the gesture, a couple walked toward the fan before being separated by a team employee. Hated to see this after the game. Fans are frustrated but no need to run onto the field and do this. https://t.co/7aPogvnfyD - Anthony Geronimo (@ATXANT10) October 17, 2026 The fan, who appeared to have field access, has yet to be identified. But Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte announced Tuesday the person in question has been "permanently banned," from Royal-Memorial Stadium, the result of what Del Conte called a failure to "represent Texas with class and respect. GOLDEN : Steve Sarkisian deals with criticism that hits close to home "I want to address the video circulating on social media showing unacceptable behavior by an individual who had the privilege of field access following Saturday's game," Del Conte wrote in his weekly newsletter . "We pride ourselves on sportsmanship and treating our opponents with respect. This individual's actions did not reflect those values or meet our standards and will not be tolerated. "The matter has been addressed internally, and I want to personally apologize to the University of Florida and its entire football program. Having access to our field comes with a responsibility to represent Texas with class and respect. This individual failed to uphold that responsibility and has been permanently banned from Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium." In his weekly newsletter, Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte formally addresses this past Saturday's postgame incident, announces that the unnamed individual has been banned permanently from DKR and apologizes to the Florida football team. #HookEm https://t.co/jdvTPGZzAr - Danny Davis (@_dannydavis) October 20, 2026 Texas will return to the field at DKR on Saturday night. Kickoff against No. 7 Ole Miss is set for 6:30 p.m. CT. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at Texas football fan banned after flipping off Florida players on field after UT loss .

item.title: Lazio Fans Respond to Fabiani: “No Truce, We No Longer Want Lotito”
item.description: Lazio Fans Respond to Fabiani: “No Truce, We No Longer Want Lotito” The organised Lazio fan groups refuted Angelo Fabiani’s ‘truce’ plea, insisting that their protest will continue until Claudio Lotito leaves the club. The Background The supporters have been accusing the Italian senator of looking after his own interests rather than the club’s. They became increasingly irritated with the mismanagement of the accounts and the recurring sales of key players. Therefore, they have been refusing to attend Lazio’s home games at the Stadio Olimpico, instead accompanying the team on their travels. This decision is among several drastic measures taken to pile more pressure on Lotito’s administration and deprive him of important revenues. Lazio Enjoying a Stellar Start Despite the Protest Despite the chaotic situation, Gennaro Gattuso’s men have been enjoying a historic start to the campaign, registering six wins and one draw in the first seven rounds of the Serie A season. Hence, they currently share the top spot with defending champions and ultimate favourites, Inter Milan. Angelo Fabiani Urged Lazio Fans to Return to Stadio Olimpico Following Sunday’s ecstatic 3-0 win over Juventus in Turin, Lazio sporting director Fabiani sought the opportunity to urge the fans to return to the stands . The 63-year-old said the empty seats at the Olimpico have been giving him sleepless nights. He also argued that a ‘truce’ would be a huge morale boost for the players and Gattuso. Lazio Fans Turned Down Fabiani’s Truce Offer Shortly after Fabiani’s words were released, the organised Lazio fan groups firmly rejected the proposal through a statement announced on Radio Laziale (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ). The supporters insist that the team’s exploits won’t have any effect on their decision, as their battle against Lotito goes well beyond sporting results. The problem lies in Fabiani’s words. There is no truce to be signed; we do not have two different viewpoints. The point is that the fans no longer want that president. There can be no truce with someone you no longer want. Many newspapers want to reduce the protest to the team’s technical ability, but that is not the case. It is something much deeper-rooted, something that runs deep within us. We are absolutely delighted to be top of the table, and we hope to remain there until the end of the year. Lazio Have Found the Perfect Successors for Romagnoli & Gila – Opinion The organised supporters noted that they aren’t the only ones protesting against Lotito, but that the majority of the fanbase. It is not just the organised supporters who are emptying the stadium. They number 3,000 to 4,000 people. There are also smaller groups and pockets of supporters who have made the same choice. That is how you reach 45,000 people. Our protest is entirely justified, right and spontaneous. The other side does not want to admit it, but they spread false rumours and other things. The supporters insist that the team’s exploits won’t have any effect on their decision, as their battle against Lotito goes well beyond sporting results. The problem lies in Fabiani’s words. There is no truce to be signed; we do not have two different viewpoints. The point is that the fans no longer want that president. There can be no truce with someone you no longer want. Many newspapers want to reduce the protest to the team’s technical ability, but that is not the case. It is something much deeper-rooted, something that runs deep within us. We are absolutely delighted to be top of the table, and we hope to remain there until the end of the year. Lazio Have Found the Perfect Successors for Romagnoli & Gila – Opinion The organised supporters noted that they aren’t the only ones protesting against Lotito, but that the majority of the fanbase. It is not just the organised supporters who are emptying the stadium. They number 3,000 to 4,000 people. There are also smaller groups and pockets of supporters who have made the same choice. That is how you reach 45,000 people. Our protest is entirely justified, right and spontaneous. The other side does not want to admit it, but they spread false rumours and other things. When one side talks more than the other, it is clearly the side that is struggling. The Away Support Continues Finally, the Lazio supporters vowed to back the team in away games with large numbers, as they’ve been doing since the start of the season. We are always there. When we play away from home, there are never fewer than 5,000 of us. We are always giving the lads our support. We are all on their side; we cheer them on and support them. We are backing an entirely justified battle that goes far beyond the affection and esteem the players and the coach deserve. They deserve the world, more than many Lazio teams of the past. We are always there. Away from home, we make it feel like a home game for them. In Rome, however, there is a battle that is sacred, and the players know that. We have never asked them for anything.”

item.content:encoded: Premier League’s Biggest Spenders 2009-2018: Where Do Man City Rank? Manchester City stepped into the lion’s den on October 11th when they travelled to a raucous Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League. The Blues were featuring in their first game since news of their run-in with the Premier League’s rule book broke, and they did so at the home of the one team that has suffered the most at City’s hands in recent times. But rather than suffering any kind of revenge, the visitors silenced those critics . City Down Liverpool at a Raucous Anfield Three sensational goals in 15 second-half minutes from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku, and Rayan Cherki, in front of a jubilant City away end, sealed a famous 3-0 at Anfield, ensuring that City’s perfect start to the 2026/27 Premier League season continued. Not only that, but online betting sites continue to make the club the biggest threat to Arsenal’s title defence. Ozoon soccer betting odds currently position Enzo Maresca’s side as a 7/2 second-favourite behind the 1/2 defending champion frontrunners, somewhat surprising odds considering City are currently two points clear at the summit. For the critics that continue to circle, the result was somewhat secondary to the situation the club currently finds itself in. Whether that’s sour grapes or not, however, remains to be seen. So, seeing as it’s all anyone seems to be talking about: That famous City spending that has landed the club in hot water. How much did the Blues splash in the transfer market between 2009/10 and 2017/18, the period currently in question? And how does it stack up compared to the Premier League’s biggest names throughout the same time frame? Let’s take a look. Manchester City — €1.44bn According to the highly reputable Transfermarkt , Manchester City forked out a whopping €1.44bn on new signings between 2009/10 and 2017/18. The spending was the most in Europe by over €300m, and the players that the club signed were a who’s who of bona fide superstars. Kevin De Bruyne was the most expensive addition. He arrived in January 2016 for a mighty fee of €76m (£54m), a club record at the time. Pundits such as Sky Sports legend Paul Merson were famously critical of the move, saying on one episode of Soccer Saturday: “I just don’t see £50million for this player.” How wrong he was. KDB would go on to become one of the greatest Premier League midfielders of all time, amassing some 108 goals and 177 assists in his decade at the Etihad, winning six titles and the Champions League as well. But as one can imagine with such spending, the Belgian wasn’t the only blockbuster arrival. Raheem Sterling arrived from Liverpool for €63.7m, John Stones from Everton for €55.6m, and Bernardo Silva from Monaco for €50m. But it wasn’t just the big names that City forked out huge sums on. Backup players such as Aymeric Laporte, Wilfried Bony, Eliaquim Mangala, and Danilo all arrived for at least €30m, with the Blues signing some 224 players throughout the eight-year period. The one major talking point surrounding City’s transfer dealings, however, is that they recouped just €381.04m on player sales during the aforementioned timeframe. They are the only club in world football to have a net spend of over €1bn, and their approach yielded results: three Premier League titles, three League Cups, and an FA Cup are testament to that. Chelsea — €1.12bn But City weren’t the only ones spending big for those eight years. Chelsea also spent over €1bn as former owner Roman Abramovich looked to strengthen his side’s standing within European football. The billionaire had already forked out a fortune on new additions prior to the Premier League’s current financial rules coming into effect. He opened the chequebook to the amount of over €600m in the six years immediately preceding City’s questioned period, the most in Europe, with the likes of Andriy Shevchenko, Didier Drogba, Michael Essien, and many, many more arriving at the Bridge. Throughout the 2009/10 to 2017/18 period in question, the West London outfit wasn’t shy in splashing the cash. The January 2011 €58.5m move for Liverpool’s Fernando Torres was a British record at the time, while Alvaro Morata, Tiemoué Bakayoko, Michy Batshuayi, Diego Costa, Danny Drinkwater, and N’Golo Kante all cost €35m or more. Unsurprisingly, they too enjoyed success, winning three Premier League titles, three FA Cups, the League Cup, two Europa League crowns, and the 2012 Champions League . Manchester United — €1.01bn Manchester United spent over €1bn too, the fourth most in Europe behind City, Chelsea, and Barcelona, and they were smashing transfer records along the way. Their blockbuster €105m signing of Paul Pogba smashed the British transfer record, while Romelu Lukaku, Angel Di Maria, and Anthony Martial all cost over €60m each. The Difference Maker But the biggest difference between their spending and that of City is that these two Premier League heavyweights at least managed to recoup some cash in the form of sales. Chelsea sold players to the value of €689m, taking their net spend to €-426m, with Diego Costa, Oscar, and David Luiz all yielding over €49.5m. The Red Devils didn’t quite manage that number, with their sales totalling €385m. That took their net spend to €-621m, still some €300m better than that of their cross-city rivals.

item.title: ‘A Suspension Could Possibly Come,’ ‘Nobody Knows Entirely Where He Is Health-Wise’ — NFL Insider on Tyreek Hill’s Hurdles Amid Chiefs Reunion Talk
item.description: ‘A Suspension Could Possibly Come,’ ‘Nobody Knows Entirely Where He Is Health-Wise’ — NFL Insider on Tyreek Hill's Hurdles Amid Chiefs Reunion Talk Tyreek Hill’s road back to the NFL has more than one checkpoint, and not all of them are on a practice field. NFL insider James Palmer noted that “a suspension could possibly come if he signs with a team,” as the league keeps tabs on the 32-year-old free agent’s legal situation. That situation took a turn last week, when a Miami civil jury found Hill liable on two counts of battery involving his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. However, with talk of a Kansas City Chiefs reunion still hanging around, the league office isn’t the only hurdle Palmer flagged. NFL Is Watching Tyreek Hill Even Without a Team Palmer brought Hill up with the Chiefs in mind, and the catch came quickly. “Everybody has Tyreek Hill circled because he’s played in it (the Chiefs’ system). You know what I mean? But there’s a lot going on with Tyreek. The NFL is continuing to monitor it, I’m told, directly by the league. Even though he’s a free agent, not on a team, they do continue to monitor his whole situation and gather all the information about what’s going on in his legal situation.” In the civil case, the jury tied the two battery counts to separate incidents in January 2024 and April 2025 and awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. It found Hill not liable on eight other claims, which included allegations of battery, assault, and continuing domestic violence, and declined to award punitive damages. Hill denied most of the allegations during the trial, although he acknowledged shoving Vaccaro during one incident. The NFL weighed in after the verdict with a statement to Pro Football Talk that squares with Palmer’s reporting: “We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer That policy allows the league to review allegations of misconduct independently of the criminal justice system, and a civil finding of liability doesn’t automatically settle what discipline, if any, follows. Tyreek Hill’s Health and Where a Kansas City Chiefs Reunion Stands Then Palmer moved from the courtroom to the training room: “Nobody knows entirely where he is health-wise.” Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, offered a sunnier read last week: “I don’t know that he’s 100% today, but he’s close, and he’ll get there really soon.” Hill hasn’t played since he dislocated his left knee and tore multiple ligaments, including his ACL, in the Miami Dolphins’ September 2025 game against the New York Jets. The injury required surgery and ended his season after four games, and the Dolphins released the eight-time Pro Bowler in February. He has shared videos documenting his recovery, but no timetable for his return has been confirmed. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Those questions follow Hill to any homecoming in Kansas City, where he helped win Super Bowl LIV before being traded to Miami in 2022. The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones took stock of the receiver room of a Chiefs team that is 5-0 and first in the AFC West, and of where a Hill reunion stands. Number two, as a wide receiver, you’d like to go to a team that needs a wide receiver. Number three, you’d like to go to a team that’s got a pretty good quarterback. And number four, Tyreek’s gonna bring a lot of impact. We’ve got to get a fair contract. And that’s always complex to negotiate in the middle of a season.” This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Barcelona starlet breaks Real Madrid legend’s Champions League record in memorable display vs PSG
item.description: Barcelona starlet breaks Real Madrid legend’s Champions League record in memorable display vs PSG Barcelona defender Xavi Espart has made history in the Champions League with the goal that he scored at Parc des Princes last night. The teenager became the youngest Spanish defender to score in the competition, surpassing a record previously held by Real Madrid legend Sergio Ramos. Espart achieved the milestone at just 19 years and 152 days, beating Ramos’ previous mark of 19 years and 251 days by 99 days. Espart makes history despite Barcelona’s defeat The achievement came during Barcelona’s 4-2 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain , a difficult evening for Hansi Flick’s side despite the individual milestone. Espart’s goal represents a significant moment in his young career, particularly given the level of opposition and the importance of the European stage. Xavi Espart impressed as a right-back against PSG. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste for Qatar Airways/Getty Images) Surpassing Ramos is also noteworthy considering the former Real Madrid captain’s remarkable Champions League legacy. Espart’s performance last night yet again underlined the obvious quality he has and his readiness for this level. Another encouraging sign for La Masia Espart’s growing involvement comes at an important time for Barcelona, who are dealing with defensive injuries ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico . With Eric Garcia unavailable and Jules Kounde facing a race to recover, the youngster could have an important role against Real Madrid. His emergence gives Flick another option while demonstrating the value of Barcelona’s continued investment in academy development. However, scoring a historic Champions League goal is only one part of a defender’s development that is progressing at a rapid rate. Espart also showcased his ability to handle one-v-one situations against Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and later Desire Doue. The former, in particular, did not have any joy against the Barcelona teenager before being taken off with an injury. Considering the kind of form he is showing, it is easy to have massive expectations of the Spaniard ahead of upcoming games. However, Barça must be patient with his development and understand that things will not always go his way. Breaking a record held by Sergio Ramos is always an impressive early achievement, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the coming games.

item.title: Ringer faces emotional marathon one year after daughter's stillbirth
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Germany's Richard Ringer reacts at the finish line of the men's marathon during the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. (is associated with: «Ringer faces emotional marathon one year after daughter's stillbirth») Michael Kappeler/dpa Former European champion Richard Ringer has said he will run the Frankfurt Marathon on Sunday for his daughter who was stillborn a year ago. April Lucia Vivienne was stillborn on October 24, 2025, after Ringer and his wife were told two days earlier that the umbilical cord had become wrapped round their daughter’s little leg several times, preventing an adequate supply for the fetus. Ringer has been running for his daughter since then and that will especially be the case on October 25 when the Frankfurt race marks the first anniversary of the tragedy. "She will definitely be there. I will see that I will give my all for her again," Ringer told dpa, admitting the race "won't be easy mentally." Ringer said that he always thinks of his daughter when he runs and that he and his partner, German-Austrian runner Nada Ida Pauer, "try to do everything in such a way that she is proud of us. "Running definitely helped me deal with it," he said. Ringer and Pauer went public with the tragic news via Instagram, and Ringer said is was the right decision in retrospect because "we got a lot of support. That certainly did a world of good." Ringer won the European title in 2022 and is a co-favourite for first place in Frankfurt where the two other German top runners, reigning European champion and national record holder Amanal Petros and Samuel Fitwi, are also present. Petros' best is 2 hours 4 minutes 3 seconds, Fitwi's 2:04:45 and Ringer's 2:05:46. Ringer hopes to improve his personal best while challenging for the German record will also depend on how Petros and Fitwi do. All three are competing just two months after the Euros where Petros won, Fitwi was ninth and Ringer 10th. "Amanal, Samuel and I made a conscious decision to embark on this adventure with only a short preparation period because we were determined to perform in Germany once more,” Ringer said.

item.title: (Video) Liverpool fans will go wild over close-up footage of Ronald Araujo goal celebrations
item.description: (Video) Liverpool fans will go wild over close-up footage of Ronald Araujo goal celebrations The old mantra of ‘never fall in love with a loan player’ is proving very hard for Liverpool fans to follow in the case of Ronald Araujo. The Uruguayan defender – still technically a Barcelona player – is spending the season with the Reds and has quickly endeared himself to the Anfield faithful with his ebullient demeanour and wholly committed performances. He was substituted at half-time in the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night, with Andoni Iraola attributing it to a tactical reshuffle rather than an injury , but not before scoring his team’s equaliser on the stroke of half-time. Araujo goal celebration captured with fan footage Araujo ghosted in behind the visitors’ defence to get on the end of a Rio Ngmuoha cross and steer a header into the net, with Sergi Cardona paying the price for letting the ball bounce rather than dealing with the danger. The Liverpool defender’s instant reaction was to leap into the crowd at the front of the Anfield Road Stand, and he was duly mobbed by exultant supporters in a moment which further enhanced his popularity with Kopites. Close-up footage of the goal celebrations shows just how many fans ran to the 27-year-old to salute him over the equaliser, in a viral clip that Reds everywhere will adore. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Will Araujo sign for Liverpool permanently? While Araujo’s performance last night was among his poorer ones for Liverpool so far, the close bond that he’s formed with supporters was underlined by the communal celebration for his equaliser. The Uruguayan told the media earlier this week that he’s quickly grown a strong affection for life on Merseyside, although he was non-committal when asked about the probability of his loan move becoming permanent. There’s still more than enough time for the necessary behind-the-scenes discussion to happen in that regard, but what we can say with certainty is that the Reds would likely be in much worse pace this season if they didn’t have the 27-year-old. His ability to cover at right-back has been massively important due to the long-term injury to Conor Bradley and the less than convincing form of the now-incapacitated Jeremie Frimpong. If Araujo does join Liverpool permanently over the next few months, Kopites are sure to be every bit as thrilled as they were with his equaliser last night. You can view the fan footage of Araujo celebrating with supporters below, via @Davolaar on X:

item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets' meltdown lets Kirill Marchenko leave happy
item.description: It took a few seconds to recognize the song and pair it with the situation during Kirill Marchenko's victorious return to Nationwide Arena . More: Columbus Blue Jackets collapse again in 6-2 loss to Toronto Maple Leafs As the video board above center ice flipped from a "welcome back" photo to a live shot of Marchenko on the Toronto Maple Leafs ' bench, the sounds of CeeLo Green belting out lyrics to his most popular song, "Forget you," echoed in the building. "See you driving 'round town with the girl I love, and I'm like, 'Forget you!'" Green sings. "I guess the change in my pocket wasn't enough, I'm like, 'Forget you and forget her too! Said if I was richer, I'd still be with ya ..." It didn't take many notes for a raucous crowd to sing along after booing Marchenko with precision, only most didn't sing, "Forget you!" when the screen cut to a replay of Adam Fantilli blasting Marchenko with a body check. A much cruder version of the song's chorus was the preferred choice of those seated in the nosebleeds, and more than a few folks waved an R-rated hand gesture at the screen. Marchenko, of course, was unflappable. He tied the game 1-1 in the first period by going to the net for a deflection off his right skate, and that goal set the stage for the Leafs' surge in the second. It was foreshadowing for a 6-2 pasting the Blue Jackets (3-5-0) took while allowing four unanswered goals in the second periods of two ugly losses within a week. Perhaps Tuesday nights aren't agreeable? If so, check the upcoming schedule. The Blue Jackets are booked solid on Tuesdays until Thanksgiving, a time of year that often coincides with them exiting the playoff race. Marchenko, meanwhile, is as happy as a clam wearing blue and white. "It’s obviously special, fun, everything," he said afterward. "I’m happy to play here, happy to be back and thank you, again, for all fans, for everybody who’s been here when I was here for four years. I have only positive notes. So, it was a really good time, but, again, I am really happy to win the game. It’s so important to me.” Positive notes? Thank you, fans? Fun? Nothing about that game was fun for the Blue Jackets or their fans, save for Fantilli's heavy hip check on Marchenko and Jake Christiansen scoring his first goal since 2024. Everything else was reduced to bloviated bluster written on oversized checks the Blue Jackets couldn't cover. The same thing happened a week ago in a 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers on Oct. 13 at Nationwide Arena, and coach Rick Bowness was excoriated by podcasters and studio analysts alike for saying the Blue Jackets should've felt embarrassed by it. This was even more humiliating, but Bowness bit his lip. The Maple Leafs had already played a game, and won, 24 hours earlier in Toronto. Marchenko wasn't the only former Blue Jacket enjoying it, either. Jack Roslovic,
item.content:encoded: It took a few seconds to recognize the song and pair it with the situation during Kirill Marchenko's victorious return to Nationwide Arena . More: Columbus Blue Jackets collapse again in 6-2 loss to Toronto Maple Leafs As the video board above center ice flipped from a "welcome back" photo to a live shot of Marchenko on the Toronto Maple Leafs ' bench, the sounds of CeeLo Green belting out lyrics to his most popular song, "Forget you," echoed in the building. "See you driving 'round town with the girl I love, and I'm like, 'Forget you!'" Green sings. "I guess the change in my pocket wasn't enough, I'm like, 'Forget you and forget her too! Said if I was richer, I'd still be with ya ..." It didn't take many notes for a raucous crowd to sing along after booing Marchenko with precision, only most didn't sing, "Forget you!" when the screen cut to a replay of Adam Fantilli blasting Marchenko with a body check. A much cruder version of the song's chorus was the preferred choice of those seated in the nosebleeds, and more than a few folks waved an R-rated hand gesture at the screen. Marchenko, of course, was unflappable. He tied the game 1-1 in the first period by going to the net for a deflection off his right skate, and that goal set the stage for the Leafs' surge in the second. Perhaps Tuesday nights aren't agreeable? If so, check the upcoming schedule. The Blue Jackets are booked solid on Tuesdays until Thanksgiving, a time of year that often coincides with them exiting the playoff race. Marchenko, meanwhile, is as happy as a clam wearing blue and white. "It’s obviously special, fun, everything," he said afterward. "I’m happy to play here, happy to be back and thank you, again, for all fans, for everybody who’s been here when I was here for four years. I have only positive notes. So, it was a really good time, but, again, I am really happy to win the game. It’s so important to me.” Positive notes? Thank you, fans? Fun? Nothing about that game was fun for the Blue Jackets or their fans, save for Fantilli's heavy hip check on Marchenko and Jake Christiansen scoring his first goal since 2024. Everything else was reduced to bloviated bluster written on oversized checks the Blue Jackets couldn't cover. The same thing happened a week ago in a 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers on Oct. 13 at Nationwide Arena, and coach Rick Bowness was excoriated by podcasters and studio analysts alike for saying the Blue Jackets should've felt embarrassed by it. This was even more humiliating, but Bowness bit his lip. The Maple Leafs had already played a game, and won, 24 hours earlier in Toronto. After flying to Columbus and getting in a nap, they backed up Marchenko in a hostile environment by skating circles around the Blue Jackets. Marchenko wasn't the only former Blue Jacket enjoying it, either. Jack Roslovic, who's from Upper Arlington and spent four mostly miserable seasons with his hometown team, scored a goal against the Blue Jackets, per usual, and added two assists for fun. If you listened closely, you could probably hear former Blue Jackets goalie Elvis Merzlikins cackling from Switzerland while his former teammates put Jet Greaves, his replacement, in too many bad spots. That's happening too much, as the Blue Jackets spring leaks with careless stick penalties, unchecked forwards left alone in dangerous areas and ongoing special teams woes. The coaches change. The roster changes. The results stay the same. Perhaps that's part of the reason Marchenko forced his way out, and why it feels like only a matter of time before Zach Werenski does the same. "It's just stuff we need to figure out right now," center Charlie Coyle said. "It's stuff we should've figured out weeks ago, you know? It's just ... it's not good. It's not the right way to play. You see the results we get. That's a tired team that played last night [Oct. 19). There's no excuse [for] the way we played. [We] let Jet out to dry, a guy who's been there for us, standing on his head making saves. We left him out to dry, and it's a shame." The Blue Jackets also let Marchenko off the hook. Instead of sending a message that he prematurely left a promising team on the rise, the Jackets got hammered in their own rink and Marchenko left grinning despite the evening's hostilities. "Good hit [by Fantilli]," Marchenko said. "It was a couple guys who hit [me]. It was great. I take it. It’s fine. It’s a surprise, but it’s a good hit, actually, and I need to be aware next time, and head up quicker or maybe [shoot] quicker. ... I’m happy to win. Again, I can take so many hits when we win the game and have the two points. It’s all nice.” In other words, forget you. item.title: NFL Players Association calls for full investigation into Jalen Hurts’ medical care
item.description: The NFL Players Association is calling for full investigation into the Philadelphia Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clots after the NFL defended the way the situation was managed. The NFL Players Association said it is not aware of any league investigation into the medical care provided Hurts, adding that the NFL previously told the union it did not plan to review the care he received. “Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred,” the NFLPA said. “Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Alastair Grant/AP Photo - PHOTO: Jalen Hurts This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: Joshua Kimmich to miss Arsenal match following family tragedy
item.description: (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich will face Arsenal at home in the group stage of the UEFA Champions League later today, but will do so without one of their most important players. Ahead of the clash, the club shared a somber update regarding the availability of Joshua Kimmich through their official X handle . The club announced that midfielder and vice-captain Joshua Kimmich will not be available for the game due to the passing of a close fami ly member: Due to a passing in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal. On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from. We send our deepest condolences to Joshua Kimmich and his loved ones. Bild is reporting that Kimmich’s father, Berthold, has passed away: BILD has learned from sources close to him that the Bayern star and German international is mourning the sudden death of his father, Berthold (57). There are likely few things more important than football to Kimmich, but family is above all else. We wish Kimmich and his family strength to get through these tough times together. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander shows why he, not Wemby, is NBA's best player | Carlson
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander mean-mugged as he sat on the San Antonio hardwood, his gaze steely, his fists clenched, his arms flexed. His OKC Thunder teammates offered hands to help him up late in the third quarter, but instead, he slapped their palms in celebration of the shot he’d made and the foul he’d drawn. It was emphatic. It was confident. So was SGA on Tuesday night. He was the best player on the court — and it wasn’t particularly close. Neither was the game. Thunder 116, Spurs 104 . On the NBA’s opening night, all eyes were on this matchup. Oh, sure, there was a ring ceremony in New York. Yes, there was a first look at LeBron and the Sixers. But Thunder-Spurs was the marquee matchup . These ridiculously young but supremely talented teams are the preseason favorites to win the championship — and as that second-quarter dust-up showed, they aren't favorites of each other — but of course, both being in the Western Conference, they have to go through each other in the playoffs. TAKEAWAYS: Chet Holmgren shows no fear vs Victor Wembanyama, Spurs as Thunder rolls in opener The Spurs got the better of that matchup in last season, but if Tuesday is any indication, a fully healthy Thunder is more than capable of handling Wemby and Co. The biggest reason for that? Shai Gilgeous-Alexander remains the best player in the game. Now, there is going to come a time when Victor Wembanyama takes that title. He's too good, too unique, too game-changing. Seems way more a case of when, not if he wins MVPs. But Tuesday’s game is Exhibit A that Wemby isn’t there yet. Wemby’s stat line: 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting (yes, 1 of 13!), 13 rebounds, three assists and six blocks. SGA’s stat line: 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, five rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Gilgeous-Alexander played all night like a man on a mission. Focused. Forceful. “Obviously, this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal,” he said in an on-court post-game interview with NBC after the game. “But for us, I think it was more, we’re just happy to be back. “It’s a long summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.” SGA likely felt it on several levels. The two-time reigning MVP ended up carrying a heavy load after Jalen Williams and Ajay Mitchell went down with injuries, and for much of the Western Conference Finals, Gilgeous-Alexander struggled. His shot was off. His rhythm was, too. With the exception of Game 7 when he was spectacular, he wasn’t himself. item.content:encoded: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander mean-mugged as he sat on the San Antonio hardwood, his gaze steely, his fists clenched, his arms flexed. His OKC Thunder teammates offered hands to help him up late in the third quarter, but instead, he slapped their palms in celebration of the shot he’d made and the foul he’d drawn. It was emphatic. It was confident. So was SGA on Tuesday night. He was the best player on the court — and it wasn’t particularly close. Neither was the game. Thunder 116, Spurs 104 . On the NBA’s opening night, all eyes were on this matchup. Oh, sure, there was a ring ceremony in New York. Yes, there was a first look at LeBron and the Sixers. But Thunder-Spurs was the marquee matchup . These ridiculously young but supremely talented teams are the preseason favorites to win the championship — and as that second-quarter dust-up showed, they aren't favorites of each other — but of course, both being in the Western Conference, they have to go through each other in the playoffs. TAKEAWAYS: Chet Holmgren shows no fear vs Victor Wembanyama, Spurs as Thunder rolls in opener The Spurs got the better of that matchup in last season, but if Tuesday is any indication, a fully healthy Thunder is more than capable of handling Wemby and Co. The biggest reason for that? Shai Gilgeous-Alexander remains the best player in the game. Now, there is going to come a time when Victor Wembanyama takes that title. He's too good, too unique, too game-changing. Seems way more a case of when, not if he wins MVPs. But Tuesday’s game is Exhibit A that Wemby isn’t there yet. Wemby’s stat line: 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting (yes, 1 of 13!), 13 rebounds, three assists and six blocks. SGA’s stat line: 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, five rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Gilgeous-Alexander played all night like a man on a mission. Focused. Forceful. “Obviously, this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal,” he said in an on-court post-game interview with NBC after the game. “But for us, I think it was more, we’re just happy to be back. “It’s a long summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.” SGA likely felt it on several levels. The two-time reigning MVP ended up carrying a heavy load after Jalen Williams and Ajay Mitchell went down with injuries, and for much of the Western Conference Finals, Gilgeous-Alexander struggled. His shot was off. His rhythm was, too. With the exception of Game 7 when he was spectacular, he wasn’t himself. More: A complete guide on how to watch OKC Thunder in 2026-27 NBA season On Tuesday, though, he put on the full Shai show, getting to his spots, sliding into the toughest areas, being super efficient while making shots behind the arc and in the midrange and at the rim. Midway through the second quarter with the Thunder in the midst of what would balloon into a 13-0 run that put the Spurs on their heels for the rest of the night, SGA splashed a jumper from the right elbow that forced the Spurs to take a timeout. He was backpedaling after making the shot, and instead of turning to walk to the bench, he backpedaled all the way to his seat, sat down and leisurely slung his arms over the tops of the chairs. It was the ultimate I’m-that-dude move. His swagger infuses the Thunder. “It’s his poise and his ability to answer the call that allows you to come on the road and perform like that,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said. “Sets a great tone for us as he always has.” That mentality may have stayed the same, but SGA continues to change his game. Daigneault said that as the team has evolved and matured, the coaches have worked to get Gilgeous-Alexander to different spots. It was an emphasis throughout the preseason. “And that looked good,” Daigneault said. You could say that about pretty much everything Gilgeous-Alexander did, and remember, this was the first game of the season. To be thrust into a high-level game right away is no easy task. But SGA made it look that way. “This is the game I love,” he said on NBC. “I work hard in the summertime. I come out here and trust my work. It’s that simple. It’s not more complicated than that. I come out here with the utmost confidence because of how hard I work, and I trust it every night. “And it’s been working for me lately.” More: Who is on OKC Thunder roster for 2026-27 NBA season? Meet the team You could say that after winning a pair of MVP awards and making a resounding statement on opening night that he intends to win a third one. No one wins any awards on the first day of the season, of course, but the head-to-head with Wemby shouldn’t be ignored. Neither should the way SGA changed the tenor of the game when he was on the court. Four minutes into the fourth quarter, San Antonio had cut the Oklahoma City lead to seven points with Gilgeous-Alexander on the bench. He checked in, and immediately the Thunder was on the attack. Jared McCain hit a three. Cason Wallace got a steal and a bucket. Then, SGA punctuated the surge with a jumper from the left elbow. Even when SGA wasn’t hitting shots, he impacted the game. In the final two minutes, he missed a three, but on the ensuing Spurs possession, he blocked a Stephon Castle drive. Gilgeous-Alexander was originally called for a foul, but Daigneault challenged the call. When it was announced that SGA had blocked the ball cleanly instead, he nodded his head as he sat on the bench. Then, he punctuated the night, the Thunder’s win and his performance. He did it with a wink. Jenni Carlson: Jenni can be reached at jcarlson@oklahoman.com. item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta has mastered the art of making substitutions at Arsenal
item.description: Arsenal have beaten Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Leeds this season thanks to goals from players off the bench By Opta Analyst They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern. After Mikel Arteta’s substitutes proved decisive yet again for Arsenal, we can say with certainty that his ability to change games from his bench is a pattern worth noting. With Arsenal labouring away at Nottingham Forest and the game drifting towards a goalless draw, Noni Madueke – introduced at half-time – won the game for the visitors , shimmying inside and striking a heavily deflected right-footed shot past Matz Sels. It was hardly a glamorous goal but it secured three valuable Premier League points for Arteta’s side. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
item.description: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history. The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country
item.description: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society The day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title. It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’ academy; Charlie was on the fringes of their first team when the opportunity arose to join Toulouse in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play.” Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
